newsitem.title: USA: U.S. LPGS firm as speculators spur market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. LPGS firm as speculators spur market.

text.p: Speculation by a trading company firmed spot U.S liquefied petroleum gas prices and led to a flurry of activity on Monday, players said.

In the Mont Belvieu, Texas, hub, propane was heard done once at 36.00 cents a gallon and three times at 36.25 cents. One player said trading company Louis Dreyfus bought at least one of the latter parcels. Propane values were pegged about 0.75 cents higher than Friday at 36.25/36.50 cents.
"When the market is flat, trading companies come in," one trader said. "Usually inventory shortages push up the market this time of year, but there's plenty of inventory."

Deals in the Belvieu hub were made in butane at 42.75 cents and in ethane at 21.13 cents. Both natural gasoline and isobutane were pegged about a penny higher at 46.00/46.25 and 45.50/46.00 respectively.
Up north in the Conway, Kansas, hub, propane deals were done at 35.13 and 35.25 while material values remained at 34.25/34.50.
Butane was done there at 40.00, 40.25 and 40.50 cents, while isobutane was done at 44.25 cents.
"It's jumpy today," one trader said. "Some people probably thought prices were about as low as they could go, so they bought in before prices got too far ahead."
Ethane in Conway was done at 18.75 cents, about a penny higher than Friday's selling price, amid a mistake that showed up on the Chalkboard system that said material was done at 19.00 cents.
